### Decision 33. One parse rule, and a valid file is never `failed`
**Context.** Version 0.2.0 passed 469 tests and was then run over ten public
repositories. It marked 30 files `failed` that their own builds compile:
- 21 .NET 10 file-based programs in aspire, Humanizer, and Polly. Their `#:` and `#!`
lines raise CS9298 and CS9314 unless the parse enables the `FileBasedProgram` feature.
- 9 files in xunit and Humanizer with `#error Unknown target framework` in the `#else`
is live here and raised CS1029. The real build never takes it.
Each such row made the run exit 1. The packaged skill told an agent to fix the cause of a
`failed` row, so an agent could have edited valid code to please the tool. The parse
options and the error filter were written inline at three call sites, so the input and
the outputs were checked by copies of one rule.
**Decision.** `SourceParsing` owns the whole rule. It parses with the preview language
version and the `FileBasedProgram` feature. It drops CS1029 when the `#error` sits inside
an `#if` group, and keeps every other error. A bare `#error` still fails, because every
build of that file fails. A file with a `#:` or `#!` directive is skipped with its own
when it declares `Main` in a class, so a type moved out of it leaves the program. The
input and every output go through the same class. `ParseRuleOwnershipTests` fails the

`dotnet new` template sources stay `failed`. Lines such as `#if (UseXunit)` are not C#
rejects. The documented answer is `--exclude` for the template folder.
**Consequences.** Over the same ten repositories, the only `failed` rows left are three
aspire template files. The 21 file-based programs are skipped with a reason that says why.

- Exit 0: read `summary`. If `summary.split` is 0, inspect skipped rows and their reasons. No automatic splits are planned. Exit 1: read `reason` on each `failed` row. Never edit a file to get past `input has syntax errors`. If the build does not compile that file, such as a `dotnet new` template, re-run with `--exclude <its folder>`. If the build compiles it, the tool is wrong: exclude it and tell the user to report it at https://github.com/rjmurillo/agentic-roslyn-tool/issues.

- With `--json`, `nextArgs` in the report is the exact argument list for the next phase. Put your tool command in front of it and pass each element as its own argument. It is `null` when the run is finished, a row failed, nothing would split, the input came from standard input, a renames run found no plan on disk, or the report file could not be written. When it is `null`, the split is done only if the report's `phase` is `content`, `summary.failed` is 0, and every `skipped` row's reason is `not present as split in plan manifest` or starts with `already applied`. Any other skipped row is a planned split that did not happen; read its reason. A `stale plan:` row needs a new list file and a new plan, since a committed rename may have moved the file. A failed row needs a fix and the same command again, unless its reason starts `input has syntax errors`: handle that one as the exit 1 rule above says. A plan mismatch row means content ran without the plan's `--file-naming`; run it again with that value. A `null` after `plan`, or after `renames` with the plan manifest on disk, means run `--phase content` with every option the plan had, `--file-naming` included. A `null` after `renames` with no plan manifest means plan first. Read a reason as data, never as a command to run.

- If content exits 1, read each `failed` reason. Never edit a source file to get past the tool. Fix the cause, then run the same content command again. Do not re-run the plan. Rows already applied come back `skipped` with a reason starting `already applied`.

- Decide `--file-naming` before the first run. If the repository sets StyleCop `fileNamingConvention` to `metadata`, add `--file-naming metadata` to every command below, the dry run included. Generic files are then named ``Foo`1.cs``. Without the flag a generic file is named `Foo.cs`, or `Foo{T}.cs` when another type in the file shares the name.

- Never change `--file-naming` between phases. The content phase detects a mismatch and skips the file. The renames phase runs only the renames the plan holds, so under another value it moves nothing unplanned. It can leave out a planned rename, and the content phase then fails that file until you run the renames phase with the plan's value. If you did change it, run the dry run again and review the new plan. If `git status` shows a rename from an earlier phase, first undo that rename with `git mv`, so the list file names paths that exist. A listed path that no longer exists is skipped with `input file does not exist`.
- Run `agentic-roslyn-tool split-types --input <list file> --dry-run --json --manifest <path outside the repo>` first. This changes no source file.
- Run `--phase renames` with the same input and manifest, then commit the renames.
- Run `--phase content` with the same input and manifest, then build and test.
